At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 [TABLE]| Programs | Minimum CGPA required to avoid Warning || BBA/BS | 2.0 || MBA/MS | 2.5 || PhD | 3.0 |

 The admission will be cancelled automatically after completion of maximum duration allowed to earn a degree.

A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

user_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?
rewritten_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

user_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?
rewritten_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

retrieved_chunks.text: Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

Bachelor's degree programs

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 [TABLE]| Programs | Minimum CGPA required to avoid Warning || BBA/BS | 2.0 || MBA/MS | 2.5 || PhD | 3.0 |

 The admission will be cancelled automatically after completion of maximum duration allowed to earn a degree.

A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 [TABLE]| Programs | Minimum CGPA required to avoid Warning || BBA/BS | 2.0 || MBA/MS | 2.5 || PhD | 3.0 |

 The admission will be cancelled automatically after completion of maximum duration allowed to earn a degree.

A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

A student who finds a mistake in the record must report it to the instructor within 3 working days of the display. If the instructor and the student do not agree, the matter is referred to the Head of Department, whose decision is final for that semester. Condonation under rule 1.21 is considered only when the application is accompanied by documentary proof, and it is granted once per course. A student who has been granted condonation in a course is not eligible for a second condonation in the same course if the course is repeated.

Students are required to maintain full attendance in lectures, labs, tutorials, seminars and discussions as prescribed by the course instructor. Absence of a maximum of 10% of the total attendance may be condoned by the Head of Department for genuine reasons, such as illness. This replaces the earlier allowance of 20% of the total attendance, and it applies from the Fall 2026 semester.

If the instructor and the student do not agree, the matter is referred to the Head of Department, whose decision is final for that semester. Condonation under rule 1.21 is considered only when the application is accompanied by documentary proof, and it is granted once per course. A student who has been granted condonation in a course is not eligible for a second condonation in the same course if the course is repeated.

user_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?
rewritten_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

retrieved_chunks.text: The minimum duration of a Bachelor's degree is four academic years, which is 8 regular semesters. The maximum time limit is 6 years, and it is extendable for one more year with the approval of the statutory bodies of the university.

When a student is readmitted with credit exemptions from a previous admission, the maximum duration allowed to complete the degree is counted from the date of the first admission, and not from the date of readmission.
Bachelor's degree programs

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 [TABLE]| Programs | Minimum CGPA required to avoid Warning || BBA/BS | 2.0 || MBA/MS | 2.5 || PhD | 3.0 |

 The admission will be cancelled automatically after completion of maximum duration allowed to earn a degree.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

rewritten_query: What is the minimum and the maximum duration of a Bachelor's degree?

retrieved_chunks.text: The minimum duration of a Bachelor's degree is four academic years, which is 8 regular semesters. The maximum time limit is 6 years, and it is extendable for one more year with the approval of the statutory bodies of the university.

When a student is readmitted with credit exemptions from a previous admission, the maximum duration allowed to complete the degree is counted from the date of the first admission, and not from the date of readmission.
Bachelor's degree programs

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 [TABLE]| Programs | Minimum CGPA required to avoid Warning || BBA/BS | 2.0 || MBA/MS | 2.5 || PhD | 3.0 |

 The admission will be cancelled automatically after completion of maximum duration allowed to earn a degree.

retrieved_chunks.text: The university runs a bus service on 6 routes covering the main residential areas of the city. Any enrolled student may apply for a seat. Seats are allocated per semester, and an application for the next semester must be submitted to the Transport Office by the 20th day of the last month of the current semester. Students living within 3 kilometres of the campus are normally not eligible, unless a medical certificate is attached.

The university offers three kinds of financial support: the Merit Scholarship, the Need-Based Grant and the Sports Scholarship. A student may hold only one of them at a time. user_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?
rewritten_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

When a student is readmitted with credit exemptions from a previous admission, the maximum duration allowed to complete the degree is counted from the date of the first admission, and not from the date of readmission.
Bachelor's degree programs

A minimum cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 2.00 is required for graduation. A student whose CGPA is lower than 2.00 at the end of the maximum duration is not awarded the degree, but may be issued a transcript of the courses completed.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

retrieved_chunks.text: Admission Fee of Rs 30,000 is payable once at the time of admission. If a graduate of this University is admitted to a higher degree program, then admission fee is not payable again.
A refundable security deposit of Rs 20,000 is also payable at the time of admission.

A waiver is applied directly to the fee challan issued by the Accounts Office. The remaining amount must be paid by the due date printed on the challan. Scholarship waivers do not cover the admission fee, the examination fee or the hostel and transport charges.

[TABLE]| Timeline | Percentage of Fee || Upto 10th day of commencement of classes | 100% Fee Refund || Upto 15th day of commencement of classes | 80% Fee Refund || Upto 20th day of commencement of classes | 60% Fee Refund || Upto 30th day of commencement of classes | 50% Fee Refund || 31st day onwards of commencement of classes | No Refund |

 Note:  Days shall be counted including working days and holidays.
After declaration of FSc/A Level/Equivalent result, admission of a student stands cancelled if he/she fails to meet the required eligibility requirement for admission. The fee refund is calculated from the date of his/her result announcement.

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

user_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?
rewritten_query: How do I get a hostel room, and which students get priority in the allocation?

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Residents must keep noise to a minimum between 22:00 and 07:00. Smoking is forbidden on the entire hostel premises. A complaint about conduct, maintenance or safety should be written on the complaint form available at the Hostel Office and handed to the Warden. The Warden must acknowledge the complaint within 2 working days and resolve it, or explain the delay, within 7 working days. Unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Dean of Student Affairs.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Residents must be inside the hostel by 22:30 on weekdays. On Fridays and Saturdays the curfew is extended to 23:30. A resident who returns after curfew without permission pays a fine of Rs 500 and is recorded by the night warden. Guests may visit the common room only, between 14:00 and 18:00, and only with prior approval from the Warden. Overnight guests are not permitted under any circumstances.

A student can repeat a course if that course has not been passed or the student desires to improve his/her grade. A student must repeat all failed courses. Students under warning must repeat such passed courses, in which their GPA is less than the minimum CGPA required for their degree.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

The Grade Point Average calculation ensures a continuous scale for the respective grades. The grade issued by the University will be final. Two types of averages will be computed for the grades obtained by each student, the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and the Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA). SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 SGPA is the weighted average of grade points earned in a semester. The weights are taken as the ratio of course credits to the total credits taken by the student in the semester.

 CGPA is the weighted average of all the courses taken so far. For repeat courses, only the most recent grade points are used, even if they are less than the earlier attempts.

 The following points need to be noted:

 "W" will appear as a grade in the transcript like any other grade.

 "I" will appear as a temporary grade in the transcript subject to change to the grade awarded. Grade "I" shall automatically convert to an "F" grade before the end of the next semester.

 Repeat courses will be indicated on the transcript together with the repeat count.

 "S" or "U" is awarded for PhD Thesis work only and is not considered in CGPA calculation.

When a student is readmitted with credit exemptions from a previous admission, the maximum duration allowed to complete the degree is counted from the date of the first admission, and not from the date of readmission.

At the end of every semester (including the first semester and summer semesters), warning is issued provided the CGPA of a student is less than the minimum required for the degree program.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 A student with a warning cannot register in a subsequent semester without approval of the relevant Head of Department or any other senior faculty nominated by him.

 After each semester (including the summer or the first semester), if the CGPA of a student is less than the required minimum, the Warning Count increases by one.

 If Warning Count becomes three, the admission of student at the University is closed.

 If the CGPA equals or exceeds the required minimum, the Warning Count becomes zero.

 For example, MS students under warning (CGPA less than 2.50) must repeat courses in which their GPA is less than 2.50 (i.e. C or C- grade).

retrieved_chunks.text: Hostel rooms are allocated by the Hostel Office to enrolled students in order of application date. First-year students from outside the city receive priority. Each room is shared by two students, and a request to change rooms may be filed only after the first four weeks of a semester. The Hostel Office is located on the ground floor of Block A and is open from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days.

A resident must vacate the room within 3 days after the last examination of the semester unless a summer stay has been approved. At check-out the Warden signs the inventory sheet. The security deposit is released only after this signature has been recorded in the hostel ledger.

Every resident pays a refundable security deposit of Rs 15,000 at the time of allocation. The deposit is returned within 30 days of check-out, provided the room inventory is complete and no damage is recorded. Monthly hostel dues must be paid by the 10th of each month. A late payment attracts a surcharge of Rs 200 per week until the dues are cleared.

Applicants submit the application form, the family income certificate and the latest utility bills to the Financial Aid Office before the deadline of the 30th of June for the Fall semester. A family income below Rs 60,000 per month is the usual limit for consideration. The Financial Aid Office may call the applicant for an interview.
